takeaways: Pfizer beat on both lines: 87 cents of adjusted EPS vs 73 cents expected, and $16.58 billion in revenue vs $15.87 billion (LSEG).
Sales were flat overall because COVID products (Comirnaty, Paxlovid) keep shrinking. Strip those out and revenue grew 7% operationally; newer "launched and acquired" products grew 32%.
Eliquis (blood thinner), Padcev (bladder cancer), the Vyndaqel family, Nurtec and Lorbrena did the heavy lifting, per the release.

It raised full-year guidance: revenue to $62-64 billion (+$1.5B at the midpoint) and adjusted EPS to $2.95-3.05, even after absorbing a one-time $650 million (about 10 cents a share) charge for its Innovent Biologics deal.
Reported (GAAP) EPS was $0.56, down 9% from a year ago, so the "adjusted" number is doing some work here. Also new: Cecile Guegan is the new CFO (CNBC).
verdict: Pfizer beat by 14 cents and raised guidance, which in pharma is basically a standing ovation. The stock barely moved premarket because the new guidance just lands where analysts already were. Solid, boring, and still waiting on post-2028 patent cliffs to stop haunting it.
